audit_findings.title: All-capex owner earnings appears to mistake rate-base investment for maintenance consumption
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 capital expenditures were $3,561.399m versus $2,049.456m of operating cash flow and $1,198.754m of net income
audit_findings.mechanism: OE anchor through the capital-expenditure deduction
audit_findings.evidence: Through our annual formula rate mechanisms and infrastructure programs, we have the ability to begin recovering approximately 95 percent of our capital expenditures within six months and substantially all of our capital expenditures within twelve months.
audit_findings.explanation: The maintenance-capex misclassification is not yet demonstrated because the record does not split replacement, maintenance, modernization, safety, and growth spending. It is nevertheless reasonably capable of changing the conclusion: deducting the entire $3,561.399m program helped produce the negative $1,267.4m anchor, while approximately 95% of capital expenditures can begin rate recovery within six months and substantially all within twelve months. A materially smaller sustainable maintenance deduction could make normalized OE positive and invalidate every reported scenario.
audit_findings.action: Obtain filed or company-supported capital-spending categories, identify the expenditure required merely to maintain current service, model regulatory recovery lags and associated financing, and rerun OE and all scenarios using normalized maintenance capital without changing other inputs.

audit_findings.title: The negative anchor makes the scenario logic economically inverted
audit_findings.magnitude: $6,398m and $36.39 per share adverse movement from BEAR equity value of -$12,967m (-$73.75 per share) to BULL equity value of -$19,365m (-$110.14 per share)
audit_findings.mechanism: growth applied to the negative OE anchor and its terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, we recorded net income of $1,198.8 million, or $7.46 per diluted share, compared to net income of $1,042.9 million, or $6.83 per diluted share in the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated model defect: increasing growth from -2% to 5% makes value more negative because the model compounds a negative $1,267.4m anchor. The resulting negative equity values are not usable estimates of common-stock value, particularly alongside FY2025 net income of $1,198.754m. The correction's direction relative to a properly normalized valuation remains unknown because sustainable OE has not been established.
audit_findings.action: Do not publish or rely on the numerical scenarios. Normalize OE over the capital-investment and regulatory-recovery cycle and rerun only with an economically supportable positive terminal base; otherwise retain the too-hard conclusion without numerical equity values.

audit_findings.title: Regulatory liabilities may be unmodeled claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: latest filed regulatory liabilities of $1,294.073m, versus regulatory assets of $741.631m; the $552.442m difference is not itself a valid bridge adjustment
audit_findings.mechanism: future customer refunds, rate reductions, or expense offsets in projected OE or the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, there were $608.7 million of deferred costs included in regulatory assets and $1,269.6 million of regulatory liabilities awaiting cash outflow or potential refund.
audit_findings.explanation: The liabilities are demonstrated, but an omitted equity claim is not. The latest balance includes $645.942m of cost-of-removal obligations, $289.505m of pension and postretirement items, $182.546m of the APT adjustment mechanism, and other amounts whose cash and revenue effects may already pass through regulated earnings. Without component-level reconciliation, the record cannot determine either the proper deduction or whether one would double count future OE effects.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every material June 2026 regulatory asset and liability to expected cash settlement, rate reduction, expense offset, recovery period, and existing OE treatment; rerun the bridge or OE only for effects not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Equity AFUDC could leave noncash construction income in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $75.425m in FY2025, equal to $0.43 per valuation share before capitalization and 5.95% of the absolute $1,267.4m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: noncash equity AFUDC included in earnings-based OE
audit_findings.evidence: AFUDC represents the capitalizable total cost of funds used to finance the construction of major projects.
audit_findings.explanation: Equity AFUDC is demonstrably noncash income, but its inclusion in OE is unresolved. The FY2025 cash-flow statement expressly subtracts the $75.425m equity AFUDC when reconciling earnings to operating cash flow, so an OE build derived correctly from operating cash flow would already remove it. No annual OE reconciliation was supplied to establish whether that protection carried into the valuation or whether prior years were treated consistently.
audit_findings.action: Produce the annual OE reconciliations, trace equity AFUDC from net income through operating cash flow into OE, verify the $75.425m FY2025 removal and prior-year removals, and rerun affected years if any amount remains.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be excess cash available to common shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum supplied bridge exposure of $520.953m, or $2.96 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: cash and short-term investments added in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The liquidity required to fund our working capital, capital expenditures, and other cash needs is provided from a combination of internally generated cash flows and external debt and equity financing.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether all cash is distributable remains unresolved, but it cannot change the present valuation conclusion at the supplied scale. Removing the entire $520.953m would reduce BASE value from -$98.32 to approximately -$101.28 per share and is only 1.8% of the $167.56 market price; the valuation would remain negative and too hard.
audit_findings.action: For any normalized rerun, identify restricted cash, minimum operating liquidity, customer-related funds, and construction proceeds, and add only the residual demonstrably available to shareholders.

audit_findings.title: A storage-facility retirement obligation is explicitly unrecognized
audit_findings.mechanism: unrecoverable retirement and remediation cash outflows absent from OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: However, we have not recognized an asset retirement obligation associated with our storage facilities because we are not able to determine the settlement date of this obligation as we do not anticipate taking our storage facilities out of service permanently.
audit_findings.explanation: The legal retirement obligation is demonstrated, but no settlement date or estimable fair value exists because permanent retirement is not anticipated. The record also does not establish how much would be recovered from customers or covered by cost-of-removal collections. It is therefore a forward-looking exposure that cannot presently be shown to alter value.
audit_findings.action: Monitor retirement plans and regulatory treatment; when timing becomes estimable, develop filed-cost scenarios, offset applicable regulatory recovery and existing collections, and include only the unrecoverable present value without double counting capital expenditures.
